title: Set Up Your Salon for the First Time
summary: Complete the essential settings your salon needs to accept appointments, serve customers, and take payments.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Prepare your team to welcome customers, manage appointments, and collect payments with confidence.

Before you start

Use an account with permission to manage salon settings. Have your contact information, opening hours, service prices, staff schedules, and payment details ready.

1. Add the essentials

  1. Open Salon Settings and Salon Information. Save your contact information, business hours, and time zone.
  2. Open Services. Add service names, prices, and durations; turn on Active.
  3. Open Staff. Add staff, save Role, Pay & Tips, assign services, and save each work schedule.

2. Check booking as a customer

Open Booking, copy the Booking online link, and open it on your phone or in a private browser window. Book an available service using your own contact details. Return to Booking and open the appointment. Check that the customer name, service, date, time, and staff member match what you selected. Check whether the appointment is pending or confirmed. Cancel the test appointment afterward to free the time slot.

See Set Up Online Booking for confirmation and notification settings.

3. Prepare checkout and receipts

  • Check the receiving account for each payment option you plan to offer. See Set Up Checkout and Payment Methods.
  • Confirm your tax rate, tip handling, and staff supply fees. See Set Up Taxes, Tips, and Fees.
  • If you print receipts, open Receipt Printing on each checkout device and select Print test receipt. This prints a sample without completing a sale.

Before your first payment

Review Complete Checkout and Provide a Receipt with the cashier. Record Cash only after receiving the money. To try checkout before serving customers, contact support for guidance. Ask which account and payment method to use. A test payment may involve real money, and completed orders still appear in reports.

If you need to check further

  • If no appointment times are available, check the salon's opening hours and the staff member's work schedule.
  • If you cannot open a setting, ask the owner to check your account permissions.

title: Set Up Your Salon Information and Business Hours
summary: Add accurate contact information and business hours so customers can book at the right times.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Make it easy for customers to find the salon's address, phone number, and opening hours. Staff can use the same details when answering customer questions.

Before you start

Prepare your salon name, address, phone number, email, logo, and opening hours for each day.

1. Open Salon Information

From the left menu, select POS (the point-of-sale screen), then Salon Settings and Salon Information.

2. Update your salon information

Select the edit icon, then check your salon name, address, phone number, email, and logo. Select Save when finished.

3. Update your business hours

In Business Hours, select the edit icon. For each day of the week:

  • Turn on the days your salon is open.
  • Select the opening time.
  • Select the closing time.
  • Turn off the days your salon is closed.

Select Save.

This setup is complete when

  • Your salon contact information is correct.
  • Each workday shows the correct opening and closing time.
  • Closed days appear as closed.
  • When creating a test appointment, you can select a time when the salon is open and the staff member is working.

Quick checks

Business hours will not save

Make sure the closing time is later than the opening time and every open day has both times.

Appointment times look incorrect

Check that the selected time zone matches the salon's location.

Customers cannot book a certain day

Check whether that day is closed or whether the selected time is outside business hours.

Helpful note

After changing business hours, review appointments already scheduled during the affected time.

title: Add Services, Pricing, and Durations
summary: Create the services customers can book and staff can add during checkout.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

  • Help customers understand and choose services more easily.
  • Give staff consistent prices and service times for booking and checkout.

Before you start

Prepare each service name, price, duration, and category, such as manicures, pedicures, or waxing.

1. Open the service list

From the left menu, select POS (the point-of-sale screen), then Salon Settings and Services.

2. Create service categories

Select Manage Categories if your salon does not have service categories yet. Add each category name, arrange the categories in the preferred order, and save.

3. Add a service

Select Add Service, then enter:

  • Service name.
  • Price.
  • Duration.
  • An optional description.
  • At least one service category.

4. Make the service available

Turn on Active so the service can be used, then select Save.

This setup is complete when

  • The service appears in the list.
  • The price and duration are correct.
  • The service is in the correct category.
  • The service status is active.

Quick checks

The service will not save

Make sure the name, price, duration, and category have been entered.

The service does not appear during booking

Make sure the service is active and assigned to at least one staff member.

A category cannot be deleted

Move or remove the services in that category before deleting it.

Helpful notes

  • Start with your salon's most popular services.
  • Use short names so staff can find services quickly during checkout.
  • Allow enough time for each service so staff can be ready for the next customer.

title: Add Staff and Set Work Schedules
summary: Add staff, assign the services they provide, and set the hours when they can accept appointments.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

  • Help customers find appointment times with staff who provide the requested service.
  • Help the salon organize staff assignments and work schedules more smoothly.

Before you start

Prepare the staff member's name, phone number or email, service list, and weekly work schedule.

1. Open the staff list

From the left menu, select POS (the point-of-sale screen), then Salon Settings and Staff.

2. Add a staff member

Select Add Staff, then choose the option that fits:

  • Link a staff member who already has a NEXORA account.
  • Invite a staff member to create an account.
  • Create a salon-only profile if the staff member does not need a NEXORA account yet.

3. Open the staff profile

Find the staff member you added and select View & Edit.

4. Choose access and payment settings

In Role, Pay & Tips, select the role that matches the staff member's work, then save.

5. Assign services

In Service Assignment, select specific services, all services in a category, or all available salon services. Select Save Services.

6. Set the work schedule

In Weekly Work Schedule:

  • Turn on the days the staff member works.
  • Select the start and end time.
  • Mark days off when needed.

Select Save Schedule.

This setup is complete when

  • The staff member appears in the staff list.
  • Their role is saved.
  • At least one service is assigned.
  • The work schedule shows the correct days and hours.
  • You can select the staff member in a test appointment.

Quick checks

The staff account cannot be found

Check the Staff ID, phone number, or email. Send an invitation if the staff member does not have an account.

Services or schedules cannot be assigned

Save Role, Pay & Tips first, then try again.

The staff member does not appear during booking

Make sure the staff member is active, has the service assigned, and is scheduled to work at the selected time.

Helpful note

If a staff member provides every service, select All Services for faster setup. Review the assignment after adding new services.

title: Set Up Online Booking
summary: Choose how customers can book online and create a test appointment before sharing your booking link.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Let customers choose a suitable appointment time themselves and give your team a clear schedule to prepare for each visit.

Before you start

First, save the salon's opening hours, turn on the services you offer, choose which services each staff member can provide, and save their work schedules. Use an account that can edit salon settings.

1. Set booking preferences

  1. Open Salon Information, find Booking Settings, and select the edit icon.
  2. Set Minimum notice (minutes) to choose how many minutes before an appointment customers must book. Set Maximum advance (days) to choose how many days ahead they can book.
  3. Choose Auto-confirm online bookings. When turned off, new online bookings remain pending until the salon approves them.
  4. Check the appointment reminder time and recipients under Booking SMS Notifications, then save.

2. Get the customer booking link

Open Booking. In Booking online, select Copy. Open that link on your own phone or in a private browser window. Use this page to check the customer's booking experience. + New Booking inside Booking is the separate option for staff to enter an appointment.

3. Make a test appointment

  1. Check the salon name. Choose an available service, staff option, date, and time.
  2. Enter your own contact details and submit the appointment request. Check the result shown before submitting again.
  3. Return to Booking and select the appointment date. Open the appointment and compare the customer name, service, date, time, and staff member with your selections. With auto-confirm turned on, it should be confirmed; with auto-confirm turned off, it should be pending.
  4. Check your phone for any confirmation or reminder you enabled. Check scheduled reminders at the time set in your notification settings.
  5. Open the test appointment and select Cancel Booking when finished. Verify its canceled status.

If something is missing

  • No available times: Check salon hours, staff schedules, assigned services, service duration, and booking limits.
  • No booking link: Ask the owner or support to check the salon's public booking setup.
  • No SMS: Check the phone number and notification settings. Use the existing appointment when asking support to review message delivery.

Share the link with customers: After checking the appointment details and confirmation status, cancel the test appointment. You can then share the copied link so customers can book.

Related: Staff and Work Schedules · Manage Appointments

title: Set Up Checkout and Payment Methods
summary: Prepare payment options and verify receiving details before serving customers.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Give customers clear ways to pay and help cashiers record each payment against the correct receiving account.

Before you start

Have the owner's approved payment options and receiving account details ready. Receiving account settings and card reader activation are separate setup steps.

1. Check direct payment details

Open Profile Settings and find Receive Payment Methods. Configure the supported options your salon uses, such as Zelle, Cash App, or Venmo. Save the receiving details and enable the method.

At checkout, these methods need to be both configured and active. Check the account shown under Send payment to before asking a customer to pay.

2. Understand the checkout options

  • Cash: Count the money received and enter Cash received. Check the change due.
  • Card: Collect payment through the terminal or payment provider first and confirm it succeeded. Then select Card to record the payment method.
  • Direct payment apps: Confirm the payment directly in the salon's receiving account before recording it.
  • Gift Card or Crypto: Follow the VlinkPay payment window and wait for confirmation before closing the order.
  • Split Pay: Review each payment portion and make sure their total matches the amount due. Confirm every portion before completing the order.

3. Check before collecting payment

Review the payment options with the cashier before selecting Pay. For receipt testing, use Receipt Printing → Print test receipt; a completed sale is not required.

Record Cash only after receiving the money. To try checkout before serving customers, contact support for guidance. Ask which account and payment method to use, and what to do if the order needs a correction or refund. A test payment may involve real money. Labeling an order as a test does not remove it from reports.

Ready for checkout

Make sure the cashier knows which account receives the money and how to check for a successful payment on the terminal or in the payment app. If an option is unavailable, check its saved details and active status. If the customer says they have paid but the order is not marked as paid, check the receiving account or payment terminal before trying again.

Related: Complete Checkout and Provide a Receipt · Devices and Receipt Printing

title: Set Up Taxes, Tips, and Fees
summary: Check the salon's tax rate, tip calculations, and supply fees before checking out customers.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Make checkout totals easier to explain and give staff a clear basis for reviewing tips and earnings.

Before you start

Have the owner confirm the salon's tax rate with an accountant or tax professional. Agree on tip sharing and supply fees before entering them; the example below is arithmetic, not a recommended tax rate.

1. Save the tax rate

Open Salon Information, edit the business information, enter Sales Tax Rate (%), and save. At checkout, tax is calculated on service charges after discounts plus product charges. Tips are not included in that tax calculation.

2. Check tips on each order

In Checkout Customer, open the customer's order and select the tip option. Percentage tips use the service subtotal before discounts, not the total including products and tax. For a specific dollar tip, enter that amount and check how much tip each staff member will receive before saving.

3. Keep supply fees separate

Review Supply Fee for each service in Services. This fee is deducted from the service amount before staff commission is calculated. It is not an extra charge to the customer. Check the agreed pay settings in Staff → Role, Pay & Tips.

Processing fees are charged by the company that handles your payments. Review them separately from amounts charged to customers and supply fees used to calculate commission.

Example: check the amount due

  • Services: $100, less a $10 discount = $90.
  • Products: $20. Amount used to calculate tax: $110.
  • Example tax rate of 5%: $5.50.
  • A dollar tip entered as $15.
  • Customer total: $90 + $20 + $5.50 + $15 = $130.50.

For this same order, a 20% service tip is calculated on the $100 service subtotal, giving a $20 tip. Review the displayed amount before continuing.

Check before collecting payment

The order should show the intended discounts, tax, tip, and total. If it differs from your calculation, check the saved tax rate, service and product amounts, discount amounts, and whether the tip is a percentage or a dollar amount. Resolve the difference before selecting Pay.

Related: Complete Checkout and Provide a Receipt · Staff Performance and Earnings

title: Set Up Devices and Receipt Printing
summary: Set up receipt printing and connect a tablet if your salon offers self check-in.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Give customers a clear, readable receipt after checkout. If your salon uses a self check-in tablet, this guide also explains how to connect it to the salon.

Before you start

Set up printing on each device used to issue receipts. Have paper and a compatible printer ready. If your salon uses a shared check-in tablet, connect it using an account with permission to manage check-in devices. Card readers have a separate setup process.

1. Choose a print method

Open Receipt Printing on the checkout device and choose the method that matches your equipment.

Star receipt printer

  1. Select Star receipt printer. Use Install to get Star PassPRNT if it is not installed.
  2. Open Star PassPRNT and select a compatible Star printer using the connection supported by that printer, such as Bluetooth or your network.
  3. Return to Receipt Printing and choose the paper width that matches the loaded roll: 58 mm or 80 mm.

AirPrint or computer printer

  1. Select AirPrint / Computer printer.
  2. On an iPad, connect to the same network as the compatible AirPrint printer. On a computer, first make sure the printer works from the computer's print window.
  3. When the print window opens, select the correct printer and paper size. Confirm that the printer supports your selected method: AirPrint or Star PassPRNT.

2. Save and print a sample

Review Receipt settings, including the number of copies, then select Save settings. Select Print test receipt. If a print window opens, choose the printer and select Print. This sample does not require a sale.

Check the physical receipt: text is readable, totals are fully visible, and the expected number of copies prints. If nothing prints, check printer power, paper, the selected connection, and any waiting print window before trying again.

3. Pair a self check-in tablet, if used

  1. Open Self Check-in Device using an authorized account.
  2. Scan the pairing QR code with the tablet.
  3. On Pair this tablet, enter a device name, a 4–6 digit access PIN, and the PIN confirmation. Select Pair tablet.
  4. Verify that the device appears as active and the tablet opens the customer check-in screen.

The pairing code is single-use and expires after 15 minutes. If it expires or was already used, generate a new code. Keep the PIN with authorized staff.

Related: Customer Self Check-In · Checkout and Receipts

title: Test the Complete Salon Process
summary: Review booking, check-in, service, and checkout steps before your team starts using NEXORA TOUCH.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Help staff understand each step of a visit before they serve customers.

Check before welcoming customers

To get familiar with serving a customer: review settings, open the customer booking link, and print a sample receipt if you use a printer. You do not need to complete a test payment on the salon's regular account.

To try checkout before serving customers: contact support for guidance. Ask which account and payment method to use, whether corrections or refunds are available, and what to do with test appointments and orders afterward. A test payment may involve real money. Completed orders still appear in reports, even when labeled as tests.

1. Review without collecting payment

  1. Follow Set Up Online Booking to check the customer-facing link. If you make a test appointment, use your own contact details, verify it in Booking, and cancel it afterward.
  2. Read Check In Customers, Track Service Tickets, and Checkout and Receipts with the team. Review each step while keeping real customer tickets unchanged.
  3. Open Receipt Printing and select Print test receipt if the salon uses printed receipts. Check the paper output; no sale is required.
  4. Confirm receiving accounts and review Taxes, Tips, and Fees. For this check, review the details without selecting Pay.

2. Try the steps after receiving support's guidance

Once support has confirmed which account and payment method to use, sign in to that account and follow these steps:

  1. Make a test appointment using the contact details agreed with support.
  2. Check in the appointment and find the customer's ticket in the waiting list.
  3. Assign staff, start the service, and mark it complete using the linked ticket guide.
  4. Review the total, tip, receipt choice, and approved payment instructions before completing checkout.
  5. Check the completed order and receipt, then follow support's instructions for the test appointments and orders.

When you need help

If you encounter an error, take a screenshot of the message and note the appointment or order number. Check whether the previous action succeeded before retrying. If payment status is unclear, verify the provider record with the owner or support before collecting money again.

After checking: Staff should know how to find an appointment, check in a customer, assign a technician, track services, and complete checkout. For any step that is still unclear, open the relevant guide above or contact support.

title: Final Checklist Before Opening
summary: Use this final checklist before the salon serves its first customer with NEXORA TOUCH.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Help the owner and staff check what needs to be in place before accepting appointments and serving customers.

Salon and booking

  • Salon information: contact details, hours, and time zone are correct.
  • Services: prices, service times, and categories have been checked, and the services you offer are active.
  • Staff: roles, pay settings, service assignments, and schedules are saved.
  • Online booking: a test appointment made through the customer link shows the selected name, service, date, time, and staff member. Its pending or confirmed status matches your auto-confirm setting. The test appointment has been canceled after checking.

Checkout and equipment

  • Payment methods: receiving accounts are correct and the cashier knows how to verify receipt of funds.
  • Taxes, tips, and fees: the owner has confirmed the settings and the team can explain the amounts.
  • Devices and receipts: if paper receipts are used, Print test receipt produces a clear sample from each checkout device that will print.
  • Self check-in: check the option your salon uses. For phone check-in, scan the public QR code and confirm it opens the salon's customer page. For a shared tablet, follow device pairing and confirm the check-in screen opens on that tablet. If you offer both, check both.

Staff readiness

  • The team has reviewed customer check-in, service progress, and checkout and receipts.
  • Staff know how to confirm receipt of funds for each payment method and whom to contact for help with payment status.
  • The owner has checked that each staff member can open the screens needed for their work.

A test payment is not required

You can review checkout and print a sample receipt without collecting money on the salon's regular account. Completed orders still appear in reports, even when labeled as tests.

To try checkout before serving customers, read Test the Complete Salon Process and contact support for guidance on which account and payment method to use.

Before welcoming customers: Review each item above with the staff member responsible. Check printers and self check-in options only if your salon uses them.

title: Manage Appointments
summary: Create, review, and update appointments during the salon day.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

  • Help customers choose an appointment time with the service and staff member they want.
  • Help the front desk organize the salon schedule clearly throughout the day.

Before you start

Confirm the customer name, service, preferred time, and staff member.

1. Open Appointments

Open Appointments and select the date you need.

2. Create an appointment

Select + New Booking, enter the customer and service details, then select an available time and staff member.

3. Review or update an appointment

Open the appointment before making a change. Confirm the new date, time, service, and staff member before saving.

This guide is complete when

  • The appointment appears on the correct date and time.
  • The customer, service, and staff member are correct.

Quick checks

  • If no time is available, check salon hours, service duration, and the staff schedule.
  • If the customer cannot be found, check the phone number first. Create a profile only if the customer does not already have one.

title: Check In Appointments and Walk-In Customers
summary: Record each customer’s arrival and confirm the service before work begins.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Welcome customers promptly and help staff see who has arrived and which services they need.

Before you start

Use an account with front-desk access. Ask for the customer's name and phone number, and confirm whether they have an appointment. Check for an existing visit before creating another ticket.

For a customer with an appointment

  1. Open Tickets and select Not Arrived to see today's expected customers.
  2. Check the name, appointment time, and service. Select Check In on the correct appointment.
  3. Wait for the confirmation that the ticket is now waiting. Select Waiting and check the customer's ticket.

If the appointment is missing, open Booking and verify the date and phone number before treating the customer as a walk-in.

For a walk-in customer

  1. Open Check-in, enter the customer's phone number with the correct country code, and select Continue.
  2. If today's appointments appear, choose the matching appointment. Use Check in without an appointment only for a separate walk-in visit.
  3. Enter or confirm the customer's name. Select services and a technician, or Anyone if the front desk will assign one. Services may be added later if the customer has not decided.
  4. Explain the text-message consent checkbox and ask whether the customer agrees to receive messages. The current form requires that checkbox; select it only after the customer agrees. Ask the owner for assistance if they decline.
  5. Select Check in on the one-page form. If the salon uses the step-by-step layout, continue to the final review and submit there.
  6. Check the confirmation and ticket number, select Done, then find the customer in Tickets.

Continue with an existing visit

If You already have ticket… appears for the same customer, choose That's me — I'm all set and use the existing ticket. Check in another guest is for a different person sharing the phone number.

Done: One ticket represents the visit and shows the correct customer and selected services. Check-in only confirms the customer's arrival. Next, assign staff, track service progress, and complete checkout.

Next: Assign Customers with the Turn Board · Track Service Tickets

title: Track Waiting and In-Service Tickets
summary: Use the ticket list to see who is waiting, being served, or ready for checkout.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Help each staff member see which services are finished and what the customer needs next.

1. Find the visit

Open Tickets. Use Not Arrived for today's appointments awaiting check-in, Waiting for checked-in customers, and In Service for visits being served. Open the relevant ticket to review its customer, services, and staff.

2. Assign the work

On a service without a technician, select Choose Tech and choose a qualified staff member. To change the technician, use Change tech. If a message says the technician assignment has unsaved changes, select Assign Services to save the changes before continuing.

A service may show Awaiting acceptance until the technician accepts it, or Assigned after acceptance. After assignment, use Start when service begins, as described below.

3. Start and finish the service

  1. When the customer is actually being served, select Start on the relevant service line. Its status changes to In progress. Front-desk staff can also select Start for the technician when the service begins.
  2. When work is finished, open the ticket from Checkout Customer. Select Complete on each finished service line. Its status becomes Done.
  3. Check the service progress count. If only one of several services is done, verify the others before checkout.

4. Hand off to checkout

Done confirms that the service is finished. Payment is the next step. Follow Complete Checkout and Provide a Receipt to verify payment and finish the order. After successful payment, find it in Completed Services.

If a status looks incorrect

  • Start or Complete is unavailable: Check the service's current status, saved technician assignment, and your permission. Complete is offered for an in-progress service in checkout.
  • The ticket is missing: Check the selected filter and whether the order has already been paid. Continue with the existing ticket for that visit.
  • A warning says services are unfinished: Compare with the actual work and go back to correct the service status before proceeding.

Related: Customer Check-in · Turn Board

title: Assign Customers with the Turn Board
summary: Use the Turn Board to see who is available and assign staff to waiting customers.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Assign waiting customers to suitable staff and keep everyone clear about who will provide each service.

Before you start

The customer must be checked in with a waiting ticket and an unassigned service. Staff must be qualified for that service. Use an account with permission to manage front-desk operations.

1. Review staff availability

Open Turn Board. Check the staff member's clock-in and busy status. If needed, review Staffs Clock before assigning work. Confirm both clock-in and availability before assigning a customer.

2. Assign a waiting guest

  1. In the view selector above the board, select Cards. If you are viewing Turn Grid, switch to Cards to see each technician's Assign Guest button.
  2. Find the intended staff member's card and select Assign Guest.
  3. In Assign next waiting guest, check the technician named at the top.
  4. Find the customer's row and verify the ticket number and service. Selecting the customer's row assigns the service to the technician immediately; there is no separate confirmation button.
  5. Wait for confirmation that the customer has been assigned and the selection window has closed. Open the customer's ticket in Tickets and verify the assigned technician on the service.

For example, choose an available manicure technician, select Assign Guest, then select the waiting customer's manicure ticket. Each selection assigns one service that this technician can provide and that has no technician yet. Review the remaining services separately on a multi-service ticket.

3. Start service when ready

Assignment identifies who will provide the service; Start records when work begins. Check any remaining unassigned services, then follow Track Service Tickets to save assignments, start work, and mark completed services.

If no guest appears

  • Check that the ticket is Waiting and has a service without an assigned technician.
  • Check Staff → Service Assignment to confirm that the chosen staff member can provide the service.
  • If the service is already assigned, open its ticket and use Change tech, then save with Assign Services. Continue using the customer's existing ticket.

Done: The intended technician appears on the correct service, and the team knows which services still need assignment.

Related: Customer Check-in

title: Complete Checkout and Provide a Receipt
summary: Review the ticket, collect payment, and provide the customer with a correct receipt.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Help cashiers check the amount due, confirm payment, and provide a receipt the customer can keep.

Before you start

Use an account with checkout access. Confirm the customer's services are finished and each service has the correct staff member. An appointment reserves a time; the service ticket records the visit; completing payment creates a completed order.

1. Review the order

Open Checkout Customer and select the customer's ticket. Check the customer, services, products, staff, discounts, tax, tip, and total. Correct any difference before collecting payment.

2. Collect or verify payment

Choose Payment Method:

  • Cash: Count the money and enter Cash received. Check the change due; the amount entered must cover the total.
  • Card or a direct payment app: Confirm successful payment on the terminal or directly in the salon's receiving account, then record the matching method.
  • Gift Card or Crypto: After choosing a receipt in the next step, select Pay to open VlinkPay. Follow its instructions and wait for confirmation.
  • Split Pay: Check that the portions cover the total and that every portion was received.

3. Choose a receipt and finish

  1. Choose Send SMS, Print, or No Receipt. SMS requires a customer phone number; confirm that number with the customer. Printing requires a configured printer.
  2. For payments already received, select Pay with the displayed amount. If a message reports missing staff or unfinished services, go back to check the technician and mark services complete only after the work is finished.
  3. Wait for the completion screen showing the paid amount and payment status. Confirm the order appears in Completed Services.

If the receipt or payment is unclear

  • No paper receipt: Use Print Receipt or Re-print on the completed order. Check Receipt Printing if needed. Reprinting uses the existing paid order and requires no additional payment.
  • No SMS receipt: Check the phone number and use the existing order details when asking support to review delivery.
  • No payment confirmation: Check the completed order list and the payment provider's record before retrying. If money was received but the order is not marked as paid, ask the owner or support to compare the order with the payment received.
  • Incorrect completed payment: Give the owner or support the order number, method, amount, and provider reference. Use only a refund procedure confirmed by the payment provider or support; editing or deleting a ticket alone does not return funds.

Related: Payment Setup · Salon Performance Reports

title: Manage Customer Information and Visit History
summary: Find customer contact details and review previous visits before providing service.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Recognize returning customers, confirm their contact details, and prepare for visits with relevant service history.

1. Find the correct profile

  1. Open Customer History.
  2. Enter the customer's name or phone number in Search. Confirm the phone number with the customer if names are similar.
  3. Select View on the matching row. Check the contact details, total visits, and last visit.
  4. Review Ticket & Appointment History for previous services, dates, and staff. Go to the next history page to see more visits.

2. Update confirmed information

If your account has permission, select Edit in the profile. Change only the details the customer confirms, such as their name, phone number, or email. Check the phone's country code, select Save changes, and reopen the profile to verify the saved result.

If Edit is unavailable, ask the owner or an authorized staff member to update the existing profile so the customer's history stays together.

Example: recognize a returning customer

A customer says they visited last month and would like the same service. Search their phone number, select View, and check the previous service and technician. Confirm their preference before arranging the next visit. If their email has changed, use Edit → Save changes and check the updated email.

If you cannot find the expected information

  • No match: Check the spelling and phone number, clear the search, and try again.
  • Similar or duplicate profiles: Compare contact details and visit history. Ask the owner or support to identify the correct profile and explain whether and how the profiles can be combined or removed before you make changes.
  • A visit is missing: Check the profile and history pages first. If the visit still needs review, share the customer and visit details with support without changing the existing appointment or order.

Done: The correct profile is open, confirmed changes are saved, and staff can locate the visit needed to help the customer.

Related: Manage Appointments · Customer Check-in

title: Review Salon Performance Reports
summary: Review collected payments, completed orders, and customer payment methods for the dates you choose.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

See how much the salon collected, how customers paid, and whether completed orders match the day's payment records.

1. Choose the reporting period

Open Store Income Report using an account with report access. Choose Day, Week, Year, or a date range. Start with one day when checking a specific sale.

Paid, completed orders appear under the date and time they were completed, using the salon's time zone. The appointment date does not determine the sales date, and unpaid tickets are not included in this report.

2. Read the amounts correctly

  • Total collected: The recorded order total after discounts, including products, tax, and tips. Use this figure to check order totals. To confirm bank deposits or calculate profit, also review bank statements and salon expenses.
  • Tax and tips: Already included in the collected total.
  • Payment methods: Amounts recorded under each method. If a customer pays partly in cash and partly by card, the same order may count as a transaction under both methods.
  • Supply and processing fees: Review these alongside other business expenses when calculating profit. Confirm processing fees using the payment provider's statement.
  • Returns: Use the payment provider's refund records for reconciliation. The Returns figure currently does not reflect refund activity.

3. Compare with service sales

Open Service Income Report for service-level figures. Net service sales are service charges after discounts on individual services and on the whole order. Products, tax, and tips are reported separately. To calculate profit, also account for the salon's expenses.

Example: $100 in services − $10 discount + $20 in products + $5.50 tax + $15 tip = $130.50 collected. Net service sales are $90. The collected total includes products, tax, and tips; net service sales include only services after discounts.

4. Reconcile and save

  1. Open Completed Services and compare one order's total and payment method with the same day's report.
  2. Compare cash with the cash drawer and electronic payments with provider records. Check fees, refund activity, and deposit timing separately.
  3. Select Print / PDF to download the report. To email it, select Email, check the recipient, and select Send report.

If figures differ

Check the selected dates, salon time zone, order completion status, discounts, and payment method first. For help reconciling a difference, share the period and order number with the owner or support and leave the original payment details unchanged.

Related: Checkout and Receipts · Staff Performance and Earnings

title: Track Staff Performance and Earnings
summary: Review service activity, tips, and earnings for each staff member during the selected period.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Help the owner and staff review completed services, commission, tips, and deductions before agreeing on the amount to pay.

1. Open the staff report

Open Technician Report and choose a day, week, or month. Here, Technician means the staff member providing services. Use an account with permission to view the relevant staff records.

2. Read the main columns

  • Turns and Hours: Activity and time recorded for the selected period. Use the hours to review recorded work time. To confirm wages already paid, check bank transfers or signed cash receipts.
  • Service $: Service sales attributed to that staff member.
  • Comm % and Commission: The applicable commission rate and calculated commission. Supply fees are deducted from the service amount used to calculate commission.
  • Tip: Tips allocated to the staff member.
  • Tech discount: Only the portion of discounts assigned to the staff member.
  • Tech takes: Calculated commission plus allocated tips, less the staff member's discount share, with a minimum of zero. Check the salon's payment records, such as bank transfers or signed cash receipts, to confirm the amount already paid.
  • Weekly guarantee: The weekly amount agreed with the staff member. It is shown separately and is not added to Tech takes. Check the salon's pay agreement when calculating the final amount due.

Example: a flat commission arrangement

For $100 in service sales and a $10 supply fee, the commission base is $90. At 60%, commission is $54. Add $15 in allocated tips and subtract $5 in staff-borne discounts: Tech takes = $64.

The supply fee is already accounted for in the $90 commission base. This example covers a flat commission arrangement. For a complete payroll review, combine this report with the salon's agreed salary, hourly pay, and guarantee calculations.

3. Check details before paying staff

  1. Select View beside the staff member to see the services and amounts included in the report.
  2. Compare the service assignment, tip allocation, and discount share with completed orders.
  3. Review the agreed settings in Staff → Role, Pay & Tips. If pay settings have changed, amounts for an earlier period may be recalculated using the current settings. Check changes to pay, commission, and tips when comparing with a saved report.
  4. Use Export CSV to keep the table. Open a staff member's detail for Print; owners can also use Send mail.

Reconcile earnings and payments

Use the report to check calculated staff earnings. Compare bank transfers or signed cash receipts to confirm how much the salon has already paid. Check the dates, who provided each service, supply fees, commission rates, tips, and each staff member's share of discounts. If figures differ, review them with the owner to agree on the amount due before payment.

Related: Taxes, Tips, and Fees · Salon Performance Reports

title: Set Up Customer Self Check-In
summary: Prepare a QR code customers can scan with their phones to check in.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

  • Let customers check in by scanning a QR code with their phones.
  • Allow front-desk staff to spend more time welcoming and serving customers.

Choose how customers check in

The steps below are for customers scanning the salon's check-in QR code with their own phones. If your salon uses a shared tablet instead, follow Devices and Receipt Printing to pair it. The pairing QR code connects a tablet to the salon; the check-in QR code is for customers using their phones. If you offer both options, check each one.

Before you start

Use a phone with a camera and decide where the QR code will be displayed.

1. Open QR Self Check-in

Open QR Self Check-in.

2. Prepare the QR code

Review the salon information, then download or print the available QR code.

3. Test the customer experience

Scan the code with your phone, enter your own name and contact details, and submit the check-in.

4. Place the QR code

Display the code where arriving customers can see and scan it easily.

This guide is complete when

  • The QR code opens the correct salon check-in page.
  • Front-desk staff can find the name used for the test check-in in the customer list.

Quick checks

  • If the code does not open, check the phone connection and print quality.
  • If the name you entered does not appear, check whether the check-in was submitted successfully, then refresh the front-desk list.

title: Create and Manage Promotions
summary: Create a clear offer, choose when it applies, and review it before activation.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Attract more customers during quieter days and times with an offer they can easily understand.

1. Create the offer

  1. Open Promotions with an account that can manage offers. Select Add promotion, or Use this template to start from a sample.
  2. Enter Promotion name and a clear description. Select Percent · % or Amount · $, then enter the discount value.
  3. Select the days and start/end times in the salon's local time. The end must be later than the start on the same day.
  4. Review the banners and where the offer will appear. Select Save promotion. A new promotion, including one created from a template, stays disabled until you enable it in the next step.

2. Review and enable

Find the saved offer, select Preview, and check the wording and schedule. Use Edit to correct it. When staff know the discount and when it applies, select Enable promotion. Use Disable when it should no longer be offered.

Example: a weekday service discount

Create “Tuesday service savings”: 10% off service charges, Tuesday, 10 AM–2 PM. For $100 in services with no other discounts, the discount is $10 and services become $90 before tax and tip. Product charges are separate.

Important: The checkout promotion applies to the total service charges. Describe the offer as a discount on the total service charges, and check the amount before collecting payment. The description explains the offer; it does not set service-specific discount rules.

3. Apply to an eligible visit

Open the customer's order in Checkout Customer, select Discount all, and find Offers this visit qualifies for. Select the offer to apply it, then check the discount and total before payment.

The offer is available based on when the customer checked in, using the salon's local date and time. For the example, confirm that the customer checked in on Tuesday within the offer's time window. Apply one promotion to the order at a time. Selecting a different promotion replaces the one already selected.

If the offer is missing or incorrect

Check its enabled status, days, time window, and the visit's check-in time. Review the offer and any other discounts on the order before collecting payment. To try checkout before serving customers, contact support for guidance.

Related: Test the Complete Salon Process · Taxes, Tips, and Fees

title: Review Customer Feedback
summary: Review ratings and comments to identify service strengths and concerns that need attention.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

  • Help the salon understand what customers value about their experience.
  • Provide useful direction for improving service and strengthening the salon’s reputation.

Before you start

Choose a regular time for the owner or manager to review feedback.

1. Open Reviews

Open Reviews.

2. Filter the list

Use the available source, rating, or staff filters to focus on the feedback you need.

3. Review comments

Read the rating and comment. Note what customers liked and what the team can improve.

4. Discuss improvements

Discuss the feedback with the manager or staff member responsible and agree on what to do next. Share only the customer details needed to address it.

This guide is complete when

  • Recent feedback has been reviewed.
  • Someone has been assigned to follow up on each concern that needs further attention.

Quick checks

  • If no feedback appears, check the selected filters.
  • Handle sensitive customer information according to salon policy.

title: Set Up One QR for Your Salon
summary: Bring your salon's customer options together in one QR code so they are easy to find and use.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Let customers scan one code at reception or on printed materials to find the salon's available services and links.

Before you start

Decide which options customers should see after scanning the code and where to display the printed code.

1. Open One QR

Open One QR.

2. Choose customer actions

Select only the options the salon is ready to provide, then arrange them in a clear order.

3. Preview and save

Review the customer view, confirm the salon name and options, then save.

4. Download and test

Download the QR code image, scan it with a phone, and test each visible option before printing.

This guide is complete when

  • The QR code opens the correct salon page.
  • Each visible option opens its intended page.

Quick checks

  • If an option is unavailable, remove it until its salon setup is complete.
  • If scanning is difficult, print a larger, sharper copy with a dark code on a light background.

title: Use Analytics to Grow Your Salon
summary: Review tips by staff member and QR station to recognize contributions and improve QR code placement.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Review tips for each staff member and QR code to recognize staff contributions and decide whether a code needs a more visible location.

1. Open the tip figures

Open Analytics. Use this page to review tips, staff tip rankings, and QR station performance. Sales and staff earnings are covered in their respective reports. For completed salon sales, use Salon Performance Reports.

Daily Revenue Trend automatically shows daily tips for the latest seven days; this page has no date-range selector. Before comparing other totals or rankings with this chart, check whether they cover the same dates. If the dates are not shown, ask support which period those figures cover.

2. Review the useful sections

  • Daily Revenue Trend: On a computer, move the pointer over the chart to inspect a day's value.
  • How Tips Were Paid: Review the payment methods represented in the tip data.
  • Leaderboard: Review staff tip amounts and counts. Use these figures to recognize contributions, alongside customer feedback and hours worked for a fuller view.
  • Station Performance: Compare the displayed top stations by tip amount. A station is a QR code saved under a name, such as “Reception.” Tip amounts do not tell you how many customers visited the salon or scanned the code.

Example: make the reception QR easier to find

If the reception station appears in Station Performance, record its displayed tip total and the date. Check that its QR code is readable and placed where customers can easily see it. Ask the owner to approve any placement change; review your stations under One QR → Receive Tips.

Record the same station's total again after seven days. For example, if a cumulative total rises from $40 to $60, the increase for that week is $20. Compare one seven-day period with another. Also note changes in customer visits or staffing, since these can affect tips.

If information is limited

Check that you are viewing the correct salon and that tipping activity has been recorded. The list shows the top stations by tip amount. If a station is missing, open its settings to check whether it is active. Refresh after new activity and share the relevant details with support if records need further review.

Next step: Choose one change to try, such as moving the QR code to a more visible spot. Record today's tip total and check it again after seven days.

Related: One QR · Staff Performance and Earnings

title: Set Up AI Voice and Customer Messaging
summary: Set up AI call answering and customer text messages after the salon's services are activated.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Help the salon answer customer calls and share offers and services by text message to encourage return visits.

Before you start

The owner should approve the service plan and messaging budget. Prepare accurate salon information, a phone you can use for a test call, and customer groups that have agreed to receive your messages.

Part 1: Prepare AI Voice

  1. Open AI Hub → Plans. Check for Current Active Plan. If you only see Trial request submitted, your request has been sent, but service activation has not yet been confirmed. Wait for service activation and an assigned AI phone number before setting up forwarding.
  2. If the plan or voice service is not available, choose a service plan and follow the instructions on that page to sign up. Then ask support to confirm that AI Voice is active and provide your salon's AI phone number. Set up call forwarding only after the assigned number is confirmed.
  3. Open AI Voice setup guide. This guide explains how to forward calls from the salon's phone number to its AI number. Select the instructions for your carrier and choose whether AI answers immediately or after the salon phone rings. Replace [AI NUMBER] in the instructions with your assigned AI phone number.
  4. Call the salon number from another phone. Check that AI answers at the time you selected and gives the correct greeting and salon information.
  5. Open Call Log and find the call. If you requested an appointment, verify its details in Booking and compare the customer name, service, date, and time with what you requested during the call.

If calls do not reach AI, review the carrier and forwarding choice. If the AI answers with incorrect information, ask support to correct the setup before promoting the number.

Part 2: Prepare and send an SMS campaign

  1. Open SMS Campaigns. If this tab is unavailable, return to Plans and ask support to check service activation. Check SMS Credits, the balance available to send messages.
  2. Select Create New Campaign. Enter a campaign name, choose the customer group, and write a short message. Check any offer link and the phone-shaped preview on the screen.
  3. Choose Send now or a future schedule. Check how many customers will receive the message, its length, the estimated SMS Credits needed, and the send time. Use only recipients who agreed to receive these messages and keep the instructions that tell customers how to stop receiving messages.
  4. After the owner approves the message, recipients, and send time, select Send Campaign. With Send now, this starts sending immediately, so finish your review before selecting it. The preview is an on-screen review only.
  5. Check campaign history and use View for recipient results. Scheduled means the campaign is waiting for its selected send time. Use recipient results to confirm delivery. Check which messages failed and why before deciding whether to send them again.

When getting started, you can write and preview the message without selecting Send Campaign. After sending, confirm delivery using recipient results and an intended recipient's phone.

Related: Online Booking · Customer Information
